title: SF1287 (2019-2020 Regular): Firearms transfers and private party firearms transfers criminal background checks requirement

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Minnesota) (gun-policy Stage 5, Minnesota); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Minnesota text (Introduction; official copy, https://www.revisor.mn.gov/bills/91/2019/0/SF/1287/versions/0/)
provenance.note: Version read: introduced (as filed). No passage vote recorded. Sections 1 and 2 amend 624.7131 and 624.7132 mainly by striking 'pistol or semiautomatic military-style assault weapon' and putting in 'firearm'. Section 3 creates 624.7134; refusing to produce the record of transfer is a gross misdemeanor (subd. 4(b)). Section 4 strikes 'yearly' and puts in 'monthly' for permit-holder background checks (624.714, subd. 4(c)); that sentence runs across the struck word, so it is described here and not quoted. Identical text to MN-SF-1284-2019.

operative_text:
Section 3 (Minn. Stat. 624.7134, subd. 2): A person who is not a firearms dealer is prohibited from transferring a firearm to any other person who is not a firearms dealer, unless the transferee presents a valid state permit to carry issued under section 624.714 or a valid transferee permit issued under section 624.7131, and a current state or federally issued identification.
Section 3 (Minn. Stat. 624.7134, subd. 3): (d) Both the transferor and the transferee must retain a copy of the record of transfer and any attachments to the record of transfer for five years following the transfer.
Section 3 (Minn. Stat. 624.7134, subd. 4): (a) The transferor and transferee of a firearm transferred under this section must produce the record of transfer when a peace officer requests the record as part of a criminal investigation or case.
Section 3 (Minn. Stat. 624.7134, subd. 5): A person is immune to a charge of violating this section if the person presents a record of transfer that satisfies the requirements of subdivision 3.
